name: Yisui Shengxue granule (Chinese herbal formula)
short: Small 3-month studies in thalassaemia (60-person placebo-controlled trial, an uncontrolled study of about 156, and 25 people with HbH disease): no adverse reactions reported.
text: Yisui Shengxue granule is described in the cited abstracts as a compound traditional Chinese herbal medicine; they do not list its herbs. In a randomized, single-blinded, placebo-controlled trial, 60 people with beta-thalassaemia took the granule or placebo for three months, and the abstract reports no adverse reactions in the granule group. In an uncontrolled study of people with beta-thalassaemia in Guangxi, China, given the granule by mouth for 3 months (155 or 156 patients, reported in two papers that appear to describe the same group), no adverse reaction occurred. In 25 people with haemoglobin H disease in Guangxi given the granule by mouth for 3 months, no adverse effect was observed. All are small, short studies, and only one had a comparison group. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
